thread:
maya: heads up — ACME Prod is seeing TLS handshake failures from their private VPC endpoints after our scheduled CA renewal last night. They reported 502s and client SDKs failing cert verification :rotating_light:

sam: thanks. any quick repro or logs we can share?

maya: customer provided this from one of their app hosts inside the VPC:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.acme.acme-corp.internal:443 -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.acme.acme-corp.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.acme-corp.internal
   i:/CN=ACME-Leaf
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
...leaf...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

maya: curl from app -> curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate

kevin: sounds like intermediate is missing from the served bundle. did the rotator upload the full bundle after the CA rotation? cert-rotator-bot, paste last upload for tenant=acme-corp please.

cert-rotator-bot: upload record for tenant=acme-corp:
- 2026-03-15T03:12:45Z status=FAILED code=403 message="s3: PutObject AccessDenied"
- 2026-03-15T03:12:00Z status=OK code=200 object=acme-corp/bundles/20260315.pem size=7.8K

sam: interesting — there was a successful object earlier, then a failed upload during the rotation window. maybe Terraform changed bucket policy right before the rotator attempted the final bundle write. can someone check S3 contents? alexa-support, can you run an s3 ls for the acme path?

alexa-support: running now — output:
```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-cert-bundles/acme-corp/ --recursive
2026-03-15T03:11:58  2760 acme-corp/bundles/20260315_leaf.pem
2026-03-15T03:11:58  1604 acme-corp/bundles/20260315_root.pem
# NOTE: no _bundle.pem present
```

kevin: that matches the symptom — only leaf+root present, intermediate missing, so clients can't build chain. why was the concatenated bundle not written? logs show 403 for the full bundle put. who changed S3 policy?

maya: customer said they let our infra team update their Terraform module to rotate the CA role. they ran terraform apply around 03:10Z. maybe principle/policy was swapped and accidentally removed PutObject for the rotator role.

sam: oncall-bot, please check terraform plan/applies for infra-account around 2026-03-15 03:00-03:15Z. we need to identify the change that revoked s3:PutObject for role rotator-role@infra.

oncall-bot: terraform apply detected in infra-account by user=infrabot-ci at 2026-03-15T03:09:41Z. Changed resource aws_iam_policy.acme_s3_write: removed statement allowing s3:PutObject for principal arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/rotator-role. Diff snippet:
```
- {
-   "Effect":"Allow",
-   "Action":["s3:PutObject"],
-   "Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-cert-bundles/acme-corp/*"],
-   "Principal": {"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/rotator-role"}
- }
```

kevin: there it is. rotator lost write perms mid-rotation. that explains the failed upload and missing intermediate in the bundle served by the ingress.

maya: remediation plan: 1) restore PutObject permission in Terraform and apply (infra), 2) re-run rotator to produce full bundle, 3) force reload of private ingress pods in acme's VPC so they pick up new cert bundle.

sam: agree. infra should target a fast apply and mark as hotfix. infra, can you also trigger a manual rotator --tenant=acme-corp --force-upload after apply? command: 
```
rotator inspect --tenant=acme-corp --show-missing
rotator --tenant=acme-corp --force-upload --source=acme-ca-20260315
```

alexa-support: noted. created INFRA-4321 and set priority=P0. tagging oncall infra to run apply now. link: https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-4321 :eyes: 

kevin: after reupload we should validate by running these from inside a test host in their VPC:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.acme.acme-corp.internal:443 -showcerts
curl --cacert /tmp/acme-bundle.pem https://api.acme.acme-corp.internal/health
```

maya: also patch our rotator to retry on 403 with exponential backoff and alert if bundle missing from s3 after rotation window. filing follow-up: ROT-98 for retry+alert.

cert-rotator-bot: ROT-98 created: add upload retry and post-rotation bundle presence check.

alexa-support: infra applied fix at 2026-03-15T03:23:10Z (restored PutObject for rotator-role). running rotator now.

cert-rotator-bot: manual run complete at 2026-03-15T03:27:41Z status=OK object=acme-corp/bundles/20260315_bundle.pem size=9.6K

kevin: great. alexa-support, please confirm ingress rolled and we see the intermediate served.

alexa-support: restarted ingress pods in acme namespace. quick check from inside VPC shows full chain now:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.acme.acme-corp.internal:443 -showcerts
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.acme-corp.internal
   i:/CN=ACME-Intermediate
 1 s:/CN=ACME-Intermediate
   i:/CN=ACME-Root
verify return:1
```

maya: customer confirmed SDKs recovered, 502s stopped. they want a postmortem and assurance this won't happen again.

sam: will draft short postmortem and include infra/Terraform guardrails: protect rotator role in a non-overwritable policy, plus rotator post-upload verification.

kevin: adding to incident tracker: INC-2026-142. assigning remediation owners: infra->restore policy guardrail, rotator->retry+presence-check, ops->run periodic bundle audits.

maya: thanks all. closing loop with ACME: explain root cause (terraform removed PutObject for rotator role during CA update), fix, and preventative steps. :thumbsup:
